validity.recommendation: Human de-dup decision vs P3957 (IGAT 1 Gas Pipeline). P0748 and P3957 are the same physical asset (IGAT-1); either merge, or explicitly scope P0748 = full bi-national export corridor (incl. 296.5 km Azerbaijani section) and P3957 = Iranian domestic IGAT-1, and cross-link via OtherEnglishNames so the Iranian ~1100 km is not double-counted.
validity.researcher_notes: This row IS IGAT-1, the first trans-Iranian gas trunkline. The evidence is overwhelming and comes partly from GEM's own row: OtherLanguageAlternativePipelineNames = 'خط لوله اول سراسری گاز ایران' ('First Trans-Iranian Gas Trunkline' = IGAT-1), and the Route [ref] cell literally reads 'IGAT-1, Iranian section'. Wikipedia states plainly 'The Iranian section of the pipeline is known as IGAT1' and that IGAT-1 (42in, Bid Boland Refinery -> Astara, commissioned Oct 1970) was built to supply the Soviet Southern Caucasus. GEM ALSO carries a SEPARATE row P3957 'IGAT 1 Gas Pipeline' (status operating, StartYear1 1970, Khuzestan -> Gilan, len 1104 km, dia 42in) — Astara is in Gilan, so P3957 is exactly the Iranian portion of P0748. GulfPub PE World Map independently lists the same line as 'IGAT 1 | Bid Boland Refinery, Iran -> Astara, Iran | dia 42.0 | 685 km' (plus a Qazvin->Astara branch). So the same physical pipe is entered twice: P0748 as the bi-national Kazi Magomed(AZ)->Astara->Bid Boland corridor (1474.5 km = 296.5 km Azerbaijan + ~1178 km Iran) and P3957 as the domestic Iranian IGAT-1 (1104 km). The overlapping Iranian trunk is double-counted. Not an existence problem (the pipe is real and well-documented) — a modeling/de-dup problem for a human.

validity.recommendation: Change Owner from 'National Iranian Oil Refining and Distribution Co [100%]' to National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC) for the Iranian section; keep SOCAR for the 296.5 km Azerbaijani section. NIORDC (an oil-products refiner/distributor) does not own a gas transmission trunkline.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM Owner = 'National Iranian Oil Refining and Distribution Co [100%]; SOCAR' and Parent = NIORDC + SOCAR. This is the wrong Iranian entity: IGAT-1 is a natural-GAS transmission line, operated by the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC), not by NIORDC (which handles oil-products refining/distribution). Wikipedia names the two partners on this line as 'the State Oil Company of Azerbaijan (SOCAR) and National Iranian Gas Company'. Consistently, the operators/owners tab already lists Operator = 'National Iranian Gas Co, SOCAR' (correct) — so the Owner field simply contradicts the Operator field. Recommend NIGC (Iran) + SOCAR (Azerbaijan). NIOC is the ultimate parent but NIORDC specifically is an error.

validity.recommendation: Drop or source the '1200' mm diameter. Documented diameter is 40 in (1020 mm) / 42 in (1067 mm); no source found for a 1200 mm segment.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM Diameter = '1020, 1200 mm'. Every source found gives IGAT-1 as 42 inch (1,070 mm) (Wikipedia's Iran Gas Trunkline article, Encyclopaedia Iranica, OSTI technical abstracts) and the Hajiqabul-Astara-Abadan Wikipedia article gives '1,020 millimetres (40 in)'. The 1020 mm value is corroborated; the second value '1200 mm' is unsupported by any source located and appears spurious (possibly a mis-entry). Flagging, not silently passing.

validity.recommendation: Keep status=operating but add a ResearcherNotes caveat: the original Iran->USSR export function ceased after the 1979 revolution (supplies cut off 1980); since a Nov-2009 SOCAR-NIGC memorandum the line's Astara reach carries only a small reverse SOCAR->Iran swap (~0.5 bcm/y), far below the 10 bcm/y design capacity. The Iranian IGAT-1 trunk operates domestically.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed real and physically built — commissioned October 1970 (inaugurated at Astara by the Shah and Podgorny), corroborated independently by Encyclopaedia Iranica and OSTI journal abstracts, not just GEM-derived. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk (Fuel=Gas confirmed). SPECS: StartYear 1970 = high (multiple independent sources). Length 1474.5 km matches Wikipedia exactly (Azerbaijani section 296.5 km + Iranian section) but that exact total traces to a single origin (Wikipedia) — medium. Capacity 10 bcm/y = the ORIGINAL 1970 design capacity (well documented, incl. the 1966 Iran-USSR agreement) — it is NOT current throughput. STATUS caveat: Iranian gas exports to the USSR ran 1971-1979 and were cut off after the revolution; the line's cross-border use since 2010 is a modest reverse swap (SOCAR delivering ~0.5 bcm/y to northern Iran), so 'operating' is true for the asset but the historic export purpose is defunct. Endpoint nuance: GEM end = 'Abadan', but the documented southern terminus is the Bid Boland Gas Refinery in Khuzestan (Wikipedia route lists 'Abadan (Bid-Boland)'); Bid Boland sits ~150 km NE of Abadan city.

routes.end_name: Bid Boland Gas Refinery (near Abadan), Khuzestan, Iran
routes.corridor_desc: Bi-national trunk. From Kazi Magomed (HacIqabul) in eastern Azerbaijan the line runs ~296.5 km south to the Astara border crossing (Caspian littoral), enters Iran at Astara (Gilan), tracks the Caspian coastal plain southeast via Rasht, then turns inland/south across the Alborz toward the Tehran/Qazvin corridor and continues south through the Zagros foothills to the Bid Boland Gas Refinery in Khuzestan (GEM records the southern end as Abadan, ~150 km SW of Bid Boland). Corridor is well-constrained by named cities; exact alignment already mapped in the GEM geojson (RouteAccuracy high).
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints/waypoints established from the Wikipedia route sequence (Kazi Magomed, Astara AZ, Astara Iran, Rasht, Tehran, Abadan/Bid-Boland) plus well-known city coordinates (EPSG:4326, approximate, not fabricated). Bid Boland refinery coordinate is approximate (~30.6N 49.9E, near Behbahan). No coordinates invented; where only a named place was available I used that place's standard location and marked it approximate. Keep RouteAccuracy=high (already QGIS-mapped); only nuance is the Abadan-vs-Bid-Boland southern terminus label.

summary: P0748 is real IGAT-1 but DUPLICATES P3957 (Iranian IGAT-1 double-count); Owner wrongly NIORDC (should be NIGC), diameter '1200mm' unsupported; specs otherwise corroborated (1970/1474.5km/1020mm/10bcm-y design); status operating with caveat (USSR export ceased 1979, now small SOCAR swap).
